title: Emergence of Double-Dome Superconductivity in the Pressurized Dirac Semimetal BaMg2Bi2
authors: Qi Wang, Juefei Wu, Cuiying Pei, Yi Zhao, Yiyan Wang, Yanpeng Qi
abstract: Dirac semimetal BaMg2Bi2 is reported to be a unique topological material that manifests surface superconductivity that coexistswith bulk band topology at ambient pressure. Here, we present a comprehensive investigation of high-pressure superconductingproperties in BaMg2Bi2 single crystal. Significantly, a pressure-driven double-dome superconducting behavior was revealed, withthe superconducting transition temperature Tc approaching the maximum values of 6.67 K at 4.5 GPa and 7.22 K at 10.4 GPafor the first and second superconducting domes, respectively. The combination of high-pressure X-ray diffraction, Hall resistivitymeasurements, and theoretical calculations demonstrates that, the first superconducting regime is closely related to the pressure-modulated Lifshitz transition, whereas the second superconducting phase emerges concurrently with a structural transition fromthe ambient-pressure P3m1 phase to a high-pressure Pnma phase.
summary: This work reports on high-pressure studies of the Dirac semimetal BaMg2Bi2, revealing a unique double-dome superconducting behavior. The enhancement of superconductivity is directly correlated with two distinct physical events: a pressure-induced Lifshitz transition and a structural phase change from P3m1 to Pnma. This highlights how external tuning can drive complex interplay between electronic structure and macroscopic quantum phenomena.
main_problem: The study investigates how high pressure affects the superconducting properties and structural stability of the topological Dirac semimetal BaMg2Bi2.
main_result: A double-dome superconducting behavior is revealed, with distinct enhancements in Tc linked to a Lifshitz transition and a structural phase transition from P3m1 to Pnma.
method: The research combines high-pressure X-ray diffraction (XRD), electrical transport measurements (resistivity/Hall resistivity), and first-principles theoretical calculations (DFT).
model_or_system: The physical system is the topological material BaMg2Bi2, studied under extreme pressures using a Diamond Anvil Cell. The analysis tracks changes in crystal structure, electronic band topology, and superconducting critical temperatures.
key_observables: Double-dome superconducting transition temperature (Tc), upper critical field (Hc2(T)), structural phase transitions ($	ext{P} ar{3}m1 	o 	ext{Pnma}$), and changes in Fermi surface topology.
important_parameters: Applied pressure (up to 25.2 GPa); superconducting transition temperatures (e.g., 6.67 K, 7.22 K).
main_assumptions: Cell preparations were performed in an argon atmosphere due to the air-sensitive nature of the material.

paper_structure: The paper systematically presents measurements of superconducting properties under increasing pressure, correlating the observed double-dome behavior with simultaneous structural transitions identified via XRD and theoretical stability analysis.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter superconductivity, the interplay between external tuning parameters (pressure) driving both electronic topology changes (Lifshitz transition) and lattice structure changes is a general theme relevant to quantum phase transitions in strongly correlated or topological systems.
